concurrency_mechanism: one worker process; activity_executor=concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=20) with a SharedStateManager; max_concurrent_activities=20. The process pool route from Temporal's docs worked, so 20 separate worker processes were not needed; 20 OS processes compute fibo(31) so the GIL is not in the way. The pool is spawned and warmed before the first rep and reused across reps. Activity task pollers left at the SDK default PollerBehaviorSimpleMaximum(5).
notes: Temporal 1.29.7, Postgres variant of the official docker-compose (numHistoryShards 4), on an otherwise idle m7i.8xlarge (32 vCPU / 16 physical cores). Config: dynamicconfig/development-sql.yaml exactly as published by temporalio/docker-compose; history.transferProcessorMaxPollRPS left at its default of 20. Workload: 2000 independent activities per rep, organised as 100 workflows each fanning out 20 activities onto a dedicated activity task queue (bench-act); the workflow worker runs in a separate process on bench-wf so workflow tasks never take activity slots. All 2000 activity tasks are enqueued and waiting before the activity worker is released (verified per rep: 2000/2000 ActivityTaskScheduled before release, plus a 5 s idle settle; raising that settle to 30 s moved throughput by 1%, so submission is outside the measured window). 6 reps, rep 0 discarded as warmup. Every number is derived from the server's event history (ActivityTaskScheduled / Started / Completed), not from harness wall clock. span_s = last completion - first start; throughput = 2000 / span. latency_p50_s and latency_p95_s are scheduled -> completed and are therefore dominated by the pre-enqueued backlog wait, not by Temporal's dispatch latency. exec_p50_s is started -> completed and includes the completion round trip to the server. Measured ceiling for this workload with the same worker code and no orchestrator in the path: 111.1 activities/s; median here is 90.5/s, 81% of that ceiling. Peak concurrency derived from timestamps never exceeded 20 in any rep.
